weeks.title: Introduction to Programming & Core Data Types

classes.title: How Computers Think: Compilers, Interpreters, and setting up the Java Environment (JDK vs. JRE vs. JVM).
Variables & Memory: What happens in RAM when you declare a variable?
Primitive Data Types: Deep dive into int, float, double, char, boolean, and their exact byte limits.
Standard Input/Output: Mastering the Scanner class for interactive programs and formatting output.
Operators & Expressions: Arithmetic, Relational, Logical operators, and operator precedence rules.
Decision Making: if, else if, else, and nested conditions.
Multiple Choices: switch-case statements and modern switch expressions.
Bitwise Operators: Understanding binary representation, AND, OR, XOR, and Bit Shifts (<<, >>).
Logic Building: Drawing flowcharts and writing pseudocode for real-world problems.
Week 2 Review & Core Syntax Live Lab Quiz.
Loops Part 1: The anatomy of a while loop and do-while loops.
Loops Part 2: The for loop, initialization, condition, and increment/decrement mechanics.
Nested Loops: Code tracing, dry-running variables step-by-step on a whiteboard.
Logic Building via Pattern Printing: Building stars, numbers, and inverted pyramid patterns.
Control Statements: How and when to use break, continue, and return points safely.
Functions/Methods: Declaring methods, parameters, return types, and execution stacks.
Memory Scope: Local vs. Global scope, and debunking the "Pass by Value vs. Reference" myth in Java.
Introduction to 1D Arrays: Why do we need them? Memory contiguous allocation and indexing.
Basic Array Operations: Inserting, updating, traversing, and tracking elements in an array.
Month 1 Comprehensive Assessment: Building basic console apps (e.g., Calculator, Number Guessing Game).
Introduction to Time & Space Complexity: Why performance matters when data grows.
Asymptotic Notations: Visually understanding Big-O, Big-Omega, and Big-Theta.
Analyzing Complexity: Calculating Big-O for linear loops, nested loops, and conditional structures.
Linear Search: Algorithm, implementation, and analyzing best/worst-case scenarios.
Array Math: Finding Maximum, Minimum, and tracking frequencies in arrays.
Divide & Conquer Strategy: The intuition behind Binary Search (Sorted array logic).
Binary Search Implementation: Iterative vs. Recursive structural approaches.
Binary Search Tweaks: Finding the Floor, Ceiling, First Occurrence, and Last Occurrence of an element.
Advanced Binary Search: Searching in a Rotated Sorted Array.
Binary Search on Answer: Peak Element detection and real-world optimizations.
Bubble Sort: The intuition of swapping adjacent elements, optimization flags, and dry-runs.
Selection Sort & Insertion Sort: Card-sorting analogy, mechanics, and inner-loop transitions.
Introduction to 2D Arrays (Matrices): Memory architecture (Row-major vs. Column-major).
2D Array Operations: Matrix Addition, Multiplication, and Transposition.
Advanced Matrix Techniques: Spiral traversal and 90-degree matrix rotation algorithms.
Strings in Java: String Immutability, Heap memory allocation, and the String Constant Pool.
Essential String Mechanics: Operations, String Comparisons, and using StringBuilder for performance.
Two-Pointer Technique: Reversing arrays, checking palindromes, and container container problems.
Basic Sliding Window: Fixed-size window patterns for contiguous subarray tracking.
Month 2 Review & Mid-Phase DSA Coding Contest.
Recursion Principle: The concept of a function calling itself. The base case vs. infinite stack overflow.
The Call Stack: Visualizing recursion memory allocation with trees.
Classic Recursion: Factorials, Fibonacci sequences, and power calculations.
String Recursion: Generating subsequences, reversing strings recursively.
Tail Recursion vs. Non-Tail Recursion optimization techniques.
The Backtracking Concept: Navigating decision trees and state pruning.
Permutations & Combinations: Generating all possible structural arrangements of an array.
Maze Problems: The classic Rat in a Maze puzzle layout.
N-Queens Problem: Constraint validation and matrix state restoration.
Sudoku Solver: Formulating advanced row, column, and subgrid validation rules.
Dynamic Memory: Nodes, Pointers, and Singly Linked List structures vs. Arrays.
Linked List Operations: Insertion and Deletion at Head, Tail, and middle index positions.
Structural Reversal: Reversing a Linked List iteratively and recursively.
Cycle Mechanics: Floyd''s Cycle Detection (Tortoise & Hare) and Cycle Removal loops.
Doubly & Circular Linked Lists: Multi-directional node tracking.
Stacks (LIFO): Array-based and Linked-List-based implementations.
Queues (FIFO): Custom implementations and Circular Queue arrays.
Evaluation Logic: Balanced Parentheses verification and Infix-to-Postfix string conversions.
Monotonic Stack Patterns: Next Greater Element / Next Smaller Element logic.
Month 3 Assessment & Code Review (Linked Lists, Stacks, Queues).
Trees Concept: Binary Tree nodes, root elements, and leaf classifications.
Traversal Paths: Pre-order, In-order, Post-order (Recursive & Iterative layouts).
Breadth-First Search (BFS): Level Order Traversal utilizing Queue states.
Binary Search Trees (BST): Properties, element validation, node Insertion, and Deletion.
Structural Optimization: Balanced Trees concept (AVL/Red-Black overview) and Lowest Common Ancestor.
Binary Heaps: Min-Heap and Max-Heap complete array-based layouts.
PriorityQueues: Heapify mechanics, Custom Comparators, and Heap Sort operations.
Top K Patterns: Finding the K-th largest element and merging K sorted streams.
Hashing: Concept, Hash Codes, Collision resolution mechanisms (Chaining vs. Open Addressing).
Hashing Tools: HashMap and HashSet internals in Java (hashCode() and equals()).
Graph Basics: Vertices, Edges, Adjacency Matrices, and Adjacency Lists.
Network Traversals: Breadth-First Search (BFS) and Depth-First Search (DFS) implementation loops.
Topological Sorting: Directed Acyclic Graph orderings (Kahn''s Algorithm).
Shortest Path: Dijkstra''s Algorithm using PriorityQueues.
Spanning Trees: Kruskal''s and Prim''s Minimum Spanning Tree structures.
DP Concept: Identifying overlapping subproblems and optimal substructures.
Memoization vs. Tabulation: Converting recursive solutions into efficient iterative arrays.
Classic 1D/2D DP: Climbing Stairs, House Robber, and 0/1 Knapsack equations.
Prefix Trees (Tries): Efficient character-by-character string storage, search, and autocomplete logic.
Phase 1 Capstone Hackathon & DSA Certification Challenge.

months.title: Advanced Java Concepts & SQL Database Modeling

classes.title: Classes, Objects, and Constructors. Access Modifiers (public, private, protected, default).
Encapsulation & Inheritance: Extends vs. Implements, and memory behavior of subclass instances.
Polymorphism: Method Overloading vs. Method Overriding (Runtime vs. Compile-time execution).
Abstraction: Abstract Classes vs. Interfaces (including Java 8+ Default/Static interface methods).
Error Handling: Exception Hierarchy, try-catch-finally, and throwing custom business exceptions.
Java Generics: Building type-safe components and generic boundary structures.
Collections Internals: Inner mechanics of ArrayList, LinkedList, and HashSet memory resizing.
Lambda Expressions & Streams: Modern functional processing over arrays and collections.
Multithreading Foundations: Lifecycle of a Thread, Runnable implementation, and synchronization locks.
Java Memory Internals: Stack vs. Heap allocation, and how Garbage Collection frees dead objects.
Database Architecture: Relational Databases vs. File Systems, and SQL vs. NoSQL environments.
Data Definition Language (DDL): Writing clean CREATE, ALTER, and DROP statements.
Data Manipulation Language (DML): Master INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, and Primary/Foreign Key constraints.
Query Filtering: SELECT syntax, WHERE clauses, Wildcards, and logical pagination mapping.
Aggregations: GROUP BY, HAVING, and calculating analytics via SUM, AVG, COUNT.
Table Joins: Combining multi-table entities via INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, and FULL OUTER joins.
Complex Queries: Subqueries, Correlated Subqueries, and CTEs (Common Table Expressions).
Normalization Theory: Redundancy eradication up to 3rd Normal Form (1NF, 2NF, 3NF).
Transactions Isolation: ACID Properties, locking modes, and maintaining data consistency.
Database Indexing: How B-Trees accelerate queries, and analyzing Slow Query Execution Plans.

months.title: Spring Boot Ecosystem & REST API Architecture

classes.title: Enterprise Frameworks Concept: The Spring Ecosystem overview.
Dependency Injection: Understanding Inversion of Control (IoC) to break rigid code dependencies.
Core Annotations: Wiring components using @Component, @Service, @Repository, and @Autowired.
Lifecycle of Beans: Singleton vs. Prototype instantiations and scopes.
Application Properties: Environment isolation with Profiles and configuration files.
REST Architecture: HTTP Methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE), request anatomy, and status codes.
Web Routing: Implementing API controllers using @RestController and @RequestMapping.
Extracting Parameters: Handling inputs from @PathVariable, @RequestParam, and URL shapes.
Payload Bindings: Transforming raw JSON payloads into Java Data Transfer Objects (DTOs) via @RequestBody.
Global Exception Handling: Building error handlers using @ControllerAdvice.

weeks.title: Data Persistence with Spring Data JPA & Hibernate

classes.title: ORM Concepts: The abstraction bridge between database tables and Java objects.
Entity Mapping: Configuring entity classes with @Entity, @Table, @Id, and @GeneratedValue.
JPA Repositories: Generating automated CRUD operations and custom query methods.
Mappings: Setting up @OneToOne and @OneToMany relational mapping boundaries.
Performance Tuning: Fixing the N+1 select problem and controlling Lazy vs. Eager loading.
API Validations: Guarding endpoint structures using Jakarta validation constraints (@Valid).
Web Security Concept: Introduction to Authentication vs. Authorization and JWT tokens.
Enterprise Logging: Using SLF4J/Logback for application state tracking.
Automated Testing: Writing robust unit tests using JUnit 5 and mocking database contexts with Mockito.
Backend Evaluation & Project Showcase.
Web Browsers: How DOM rendering engines read source structures. Semantic HTML5 tags.
CSS Specificity: The Cascading inheritance engine, selectors, and the CSS Box Model layout.
Flexbox Engine: Master directional alignment controls along main and cross axes.
Grid Layouts: Advanced multi-dimensional layout sheets, grid templates, and areas.
Responsive Web: Building media queries, fluid sizing viewports, and modern CSS variables.
JavaScript Basics: Variable lifecycles (var, let, const), implicit conversions, and dynamic data typing.
Scopes & Execution Context: Scoping chains, Closures, and how the compilation phase hoists declarations.
First-Class Functions: Callbacks, Arrow Functions, and High-Order arrays mappings.
Complex Types: Array structures mutation methods (map(), filter(), reduce()) and Object states.
Modern ES6+ Tooling: Destructuring assignments, Spread operators, and Template Strings.
DOM APIs: Dynamic document generation, node selection query selectors, and modifying markup.
Event Engine: Binding listeners, Event Bubbling propagation paths, and Event Delegation strategies.
Asynchronous Event Loop: Call Stacks, Web APIs, Task Queues, and the event processing cycle.
Promises Lifecycle: Creating, chaining, and error-catching on async pipelines.
Async/Await Syntax: Writing cleaner async flows with try-catch blocks.
Network API Integration: Fetching raw REST payloads using the browser''s Fetch API.
Browser Storage: Using localStorage, sessionStorage, and setting cookies.
Node Tooling: Managing dependencies through npm or yarn environments.
Version Control: Git repository setups, remote synchronization, branching, and pull requests on GitHub.
Month 7 Project Showcase: Building a modular data dashboard application using pure Vanilla JS.

months.title: Component Architecture with React.js & Full-Stack Assembly

classes.title: Declarative UI Concept: Comparing React''s state rendering loop against imperative Vanilla structures.
Vite Project Bootstrapping: Exploring structural assets, package maps, and compilation tasks.
JSX Mechanics: Rules of element compilation, fragment abstractions, and attribute mapping.
Functional Components: Passing properties (props) down component trees as immutable inputs.
Iterative Components: Mapping item arrays into lists while retaining strict key attributes.
State Engine: Declaring mutable UI values inside components with the useState hook.
User Input Forms: Creating controlled form components vs. uncontrolled inputs.
Handling Side Effects: Utilizing the useEffect hook, controlling execution with dependency arrays, and cleanup tasks.
Data Subscriptions: Calling distant Spring Boot backend APIs directly inside component hooks.
Custom Hooks: Abstracting heavy data tracking or event logic out of UI view files.
Client Routing: Configuring client-side routes using React Router DOM.
Dynamic URL Routing: Parsing variables using useParams and updating query tracking strings.
Global Contexts: Stopping prop drilling limitations by configuring global application contexts with useContext.
Code Optimization: Managing rendering recalculation limits via useMemo and useCallback hook checks.
UI Frameworks: Integrating style frameworks like Tailwind CSS into the React rendering flow.
System Plumbing: Routing frontend network calls directly to the localized Spring Boot endpoints.
Cross-Origin Control: Configuring CORS policy variables inside Java configuration filters to accept external client queries.
Secure Interceptors: Attaching JWT verification tokens to client request headers.
Deployment Engines: Uploading static UI components to Vercel/Netlify, and host servers for databases.
Final Capstone Reviews & Graduation Project Evaluations.
